short: Attempted handwriting (M04) is a new text-entry action, but one participant; label timing (M02) and decoder (M06) are standard; the >99% headline relies on an offline language model.
position: The paper changes the use-time action (M04), the training label timing (M02) and the decoder (M06) [@willett2021handwriting]. The action is new: none of the 36 studies dated 2020 or earlier in the 154-study neural text-entry population names attempted handwriting (pattern match, Appendix), and 90 raw characters per minute in copy typing more than double the 39.2 correct characters per minute the same participant reached by point-and-click [@pandarinath2017communication]. All three are standard under the verdict rules: the evidence is one participant, CTC already removed frame labels [@sun2020brain2char], and the successor speech BCI uses it [@willett2023speech]. The >99% offline headline rests on a retrospective bigram model with an unstated corpus; the online word error rate was 25.1%. The free-typing benchmark it beats belongs to another participant, and the system had no backspace. Attempted speech at 62 words per minute [@willett2023speech] and finger typing at 110 characters per minute [@jude2026bimanual] [later] have since overtaken it.
